description: This file defines the KeyEventStateMachine class, which manages key event sequences and state transitions for an on-screen keyboard input method. It includes internal classes for state management, transition handling, and a ring buffer implementation to process key sequences and match input patterns.

classes.name: KeyEventStateMachine
classes.description: Main class managing key event sequences and state transitions.

classes.name: KeyEventStateMachine.State
classes.description: Enumeration representing the possible states of key sequence matching.

classes.name: KeyEventStateMachine.KeyEventTransition
classes.description: Internal class representing a transition from one key event state to another based on a key code.

classes.name: KeyEventStateMachine.KeyEventState
classes.description: Internal class representing a state in the key event state machine, with transitions and result code.

classes.name: KeyEventStateMachine.NFAPart
classes.description: Internal class representing a part of the NFA (Non-deterministic Finite Automaton) used for sequence matching.

classes.name: KeyEventStateMachine.RingBuffer
classes.description: Ring buffer implementation for managing NFAPart objects during sequence processing.

methods.name: addNextState
methods.description: Creates or retrieves the next state for a given key code from the current state.

methods.name: addSequence
methods.description: Adds a key sequence with an associated result character to the state machine.

methods.name: addSpecialKeySequence
methods.description: Adds a key sequence with a special key and result character to the state machine.

methods.name: addKeyCode
methods.description: Processes a key code input, updating the state machine and returning the match result.

methods.name: getCharacter
methods.description: Returns the result character of the last matched sequence.

methods.name: getSequenceLength
methods.description: Returns the length of the matched sequence.

methods.name: reset
methods.description: Resets the state machine to its initial state.
